rubric_notes: All five a.22.1 families correctly enumerated with sunids and protein members, all supported by bundle children/annotations/homology endpoints. Correctly interprets superfamily as probable common ancestry, family as closer relationship, and notes fold-level warning is moot because a.22 has one superfamily. Explicitly states function (DNA wrapping, GEF activity, etc.) does not transfer across families and flags automated-match status. Clear limits section. Freeze date is correct though not in its bundle; not penalized. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

All classifications, sunids, boundaries (1y6x A:7-93) and annotation comments match the bundle. Identifies superfamily as lowest shared node, frames relationship as remote homology stronger than fold but weaker than family, and explicitly refuses to transfer PR-ATP or MazG substrate, pathway, oligomeric state, or template suitability. Notes unverified function of the hypothetical Sulfolobus protein and absence of quality/historical data. Complete.

Correct families c.55.1.1/c.55.1.3/c.55.1.4 in c.55.1 with correct sunids, fold/class, duplication comment, and homology flags all supported by the bundle. Infers probable common ancestry and conserved two-lobe nucleotide-binding core, explicitly rejects transfer of substrate, chemistry, catalytic residues, regulation, oligomeric/filament state, cellular role, and template interchangeability; correctly treats fold-level neighbours as neither homologous nor convergent. Example domain SIDs/boundaries (d1atna1/2, d3hsca1/2, d1ig8a1/2, d1glcg1/2) are not in the bundle but are consistent with known SCOPe splits; no material error found. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Complete and fully supported: correct hierarchy, sunids, family members, comments, homology scopes, and release/periodic labels; interprets as shared ancestral scaffold recruited to divergent chemistries, explicitly not functional equivalence; refuses transfer of substrate, metal, oligomer, or template; correctly withholds nonhomology claims for other a.25 superfamilies and notes API does not expose curatorial rationale. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Complete and accurate: families, superfamily, sunids, Pfam, domains and comments all match bundle; same_superfamily relationship derivable from retrieved parents. Interpretation distinguishes superfamily homology from family-level relationship, refuses copper/ET transfer citing lacking-metal-site annotations, and gives thorough limits. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Families, sunids, Pfam xrefs, sibling families, 15 fold superfamilies, homology flags and member lists supported by bundle. Correct two-level interpretation (family = close relationship, superfamily = probable common origin), fold-level absence not strengthened to convergence. Enumerates unsafe transfers: modifier/conjugation to UBX/RBD, Ras binding to other families and within-RBD specificity, p97 binding, sibling families, interface templates, non-conjugated UBL domains, MoaD/ThiS; requires external evidence; notes automated-match provenance. Minor unverifiable Ubl3/Ubl5, SUMO-3.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. Correct families/sunids/domains; places ODC catalysis in d1orda2 (c.67.1.5) and d1orda3 (d.125.1.1) and KaiA clock function in d1r8ja1 (a.186.1.1), which are the actual SCOPe placements (c.67.1.5 lineage was queried but omitted from the bundle for size; boundaries match SCOP's 1ord domain definitions). Superfamily-strength ancestry stated, fold-level similarity explicitly insufficient, phosphoacceptor signaling, decarboxylase activity, and circadian function all rejected for cross-family transfer, 'complexed with plp' correctly interpreted. Minor: pairwise 'same_superfamily' comparison claim is not in the bundle but is derivable from parents.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. Verified b.84.5 (310577) under b.84 (51229), b.84.5.1 (310616), two protein entries with correct example domains and boundaries, five superfamilies with sunids/comments, PubMed xref, fold homology warning. Explicitly asymmetric: positive family-level homology between V-type and A-type bulges, fold-level similarity only toward b.84.1-b.84.4, no negative (analogy/convergence) claim. Honest that curatorial rationale is not exposed by the API. Rejects function transfer from b.84.1 and notes boundary differences between members. Concise but covers all must-include items and scoring foci.

Correct: fold f.21 with three separate superfamilies f.21.1/f.21.2/f.21.3 (sunids and families match bundle); uses homology endpoint (fold false, sf true) to distinguish fold from superfamily; cites f.21.3 'possible link' comment and explicitly declines to assert non-homology; lists sequence/profile, heme-ligand/topology, and phylogenetic evidence needed. No material errors.

Identifiers, family membership, fold-level warning, representative domains d1n8ka2, d2nu8a1 and d1id1a_ with their lineages and annotations (including the automated match and CoA-complex comments) are all present in the bundle. Correctly states that the lowest shared node is the superfamily, that this is a probable-ancestry claim distinct from family-level closeness, and that fold/class add only architecture. Rejects transfer of function, ligand and templates, declines to make a best-structure claim without SPACI/AEROSPACI, and warns against strengthening the c.3/c.4 similarity note into either homology or convergence. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Complete: same family k.40.1.1 (sunid 100905), 'not a true family' comment cited as the decisive caveat overriding the mechanical same-family reading, class k context, fold/class warnings supported by bundle. Calibrated: notes SCOPe does not assert homology and also does not prove a negative. Clear unsafe-transfer limits and external-evidence needs. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-14. Meets all must_include: 1.69 lineages for both domains verified (c.137.1.1 vs c.23.14.1, superfamily then named N-deoxyribosyltransferase); 2.08 d1t1ja1/d1f8ya_ in c.23.14.2/c.23.14.1 under renamed superfamily verified; states move from no asserted relationship to probable common ancestry, with stable sunids re-parented, so a reclassification not a new entry. Correctly separates the artifact-tag split (class l, artifact_not_homology_evidence warning in bundle) from the evolutionary change. 1.71/1.73 placement claims not in this bundle but are correct. Function-transfer and template caveats present; notes curator rationale not exposed by API.

Complete and supported: both segments correctly classified with boundaries, homology responses for both SIDs cited accurately, clear rejection of tag similarity as homology, notes 'Synthetic' species must not be mapped to an organism, states limits on tag sequence. No material errors.

Accurate 1.75 whole-chain record and accurate split with correct sunids, sccs, and boundaries, bracketed to 2.04 onward with the retired old superfamily node noted. Strong modularity inference from the recurrence of the N-terminal unit in another kingdom and in a glycoside hydrolase context, with explicit refusal of bidirectional function transfer, correct handling of different classes as absence of assertion, and a note that the two domains do not tile the chain. Quotes a cluster representative with identity and coverage figures not supported by the retrieved evidence.

All must_include criteria met with correct identifiers and boundaries; 1.75 lookup of family 159638 supports pre-existence of the RNase H-like family; d.394 singleton lineage verified. Interpretation covers mosaic evolution, domain reuse vs innovation, superfamily vs family strength, and explicit refusal to transfer polymerase/nuclease/acetyl-lysine function. Limits stated.

All three must-include elements present: common family a.298.1.1, length as repeat copy number in a tandem array kept as one domain, and explicit use of the 're' heterogeneity code plus the family-level canonical repeat record with representative d4cj9a_. Correctly restricts 259-292 to 4cj9 numbering, labels derived repeat counts as inference, notes absence of a caveat is not positive evidence, declines quality ranking without SPACI/AEROSPACI, and scopes everything to 2.08. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

All reported fields match evidence. Cites stable 2.08 selector pinned in release-scoped calls, rejects unpinned 'current', explains periodic label format and that it does not replace stable, and preserves the exact dated label when post-freeze records are used. Endpoint limits and is_comprehensive caveat correctly stated.

Evaluator Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. Verified lineage and the 1.75-to-2.08 change (ms flag added; d1dn1b_ from curated sunid 17771 to automated match sunid 302344 under 'automated matches'). Reasoning: homology unchanged at family level, fold assignment inherited from complete domain because a three-helix fragment cannot show the four-helix a.47 topology, spectrin comment treated as a warning without homology/analogy claim, d3c98b_ as curated complete reference, function not transferable from family. Limits honestly stated (quality not retrieved, rationale not exposed). No material errors.

Evaluator Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. Reasoning is complete: divergence within c.2.1, asymmetric statement for cross-fold cases, c.4.1 'link' comment used correctly as evidence curators considered remote relationship plausible, ribokinase-like c.72 comment as an apt parallel, full evidence-integration list and explicit limits. Factual slip: lists c.58 (amino-acid dehydrogenase N-terminal, substrate domain) and c.23.12 (formate/glycerate DH catalytic domain) among folds where NAD(P)/FAD binding occurs, though it later correctly notes the NAD domain is the c.2.1.4 partner. All sunids, comments and homology values otherwise match the bundle.

Complete on both required release states with correct nodes, the 404s confirming the retired b.23.2 and the new b.18.1.36, and the chain B boundary plus artifact change kept distinct from the homology decision. Evidence is layered and correctly weighted: the curated PubMed 17977833 note with its Cry4Ba and enterotoxin partners, a graded structure-comparison ladder across b.18.1 families reported explicitly as representative-derived from 1nqjA, the diagnostic absence of sequence support as a sign of remoteness rather than non-relationship, and compatible accessory-module function labeled as interpretation. Limits section bars function, calcium and template transfer, refuses to treat filtered absence as counter-evidence, and declines to convert missing warnings into positive support.

All lineage, sunid, comment, hf and homology facts match the bundle. States family/protein/species-level homology survives, hf means a different fold despite similar sequence and SSE count, and that d1ztra1 must not serve as fold template or a.4 positive; recommends exclusion or stratification with the flag preserved. Correctly declines quality ranking because quality fields were not retrieved and names needed external evidence.

Lineage, fr flag (domain scope, non-inherited), comment, ATOM-derived 50/99 residues vs 104, and quality values all consistent with the bundle (1o5d quality and 218-residue SEQRES not in this bundle but correct). Clearly states homology is unaffected, that alignment coverage/scores against the fragment reflect missing strands not divergence, that SPACI would wrongly favour the fragment, that complete domains are compared for representatives with d1uc6a1's NMR caveat, that the fr label should be carried through and sensitivity tested, and that function is not transferred. Honest about not retrieving d1o5dt1 annotations. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-14.

Biological reasoning complete: new superfamily in existing fold; family = positive probable-homology claim requiring integrated evidence (rejected); superfamily split asymmetric and provisional, not a non-homology verdict; new fold only for different arrangement/topology or nf/hf cases. Rejects function/template transfer; notes manual curation and revision path. Factual deduction: attributes release 2.08 details (freeze, release, 2.08-2026-08-16) to 'the SCOPe service' but the evidence bundle is empty, so that API-dependent claim is unsupported (noncentral). Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-14.

Correct classification with bundle-supported sunids, family children (ThrB, MtnK, RdoA; mTOR in PI3K family), homology endpoints and comments. Correctly distinguishes superfamily-level probable homology from family-level closeness; uses APH family heterogeneity to show even family placement does not fix substrate. Explicitly rejects substrate, regulation, inhibitor and template transfer. Evidence list includes alignments with catalytic motifs, FATCAT structural alignment, ligand-bound structures, domain/genomic context, phylogeny and biochemical assays. No material errors.
